# Sharp nonheavy threshold for the original midpoint residual row

The root proposed the statement below. This note independently proves
its constants, repairs the residual boundary convention, and gives exact
sharp examples. This is a local theorem for three full-dimensional
fibers, not a proof of OC.

## 1. Statement and exact constants

Fix d>=1. Let A,K,R be compact convex bodies in R^d with

    (A+R)/2 subset K.

Write their positive volume roots as a,c,b, respectively, and set

    M=a^d+c^d+b^d.

Assume that no one of the three fiber volumes exceeds M/2. Place them
at integer bases -1,0,1. For an arbitrary closed ambient halfspace H
in R times R^d define

    p=|K intersect H_0|/|K|,
    f_-=|A minus H_-1|^(1/d),
    f_0=|K minus H_0|^(1/d)=c(1-p)^(1/d),
    f_+=|R minus H_1|^(1/d).

Residuals mean the strict complements of the CLOSED cap. This retains
the identity for f_0 even when a purely integer cap has the entire
middle fiber on its boundary.

Let B_d be the unique number in (1,2) solving

    B_d^d-(2-B_d)^d=1,                                (1)

and put

    eta_d=1-(B_d/2)^d.

Then

    [(f_-+f_+)/2-f_0]_+
       <=c[B_d/2-(1-p)^(1/d)]_+.                      (2)

In particular, if p<=eta_d, then the ORIGINAL midpoint row obeys

    f_0>=(f_-+f_+)/2.                                (3)

The threshold and the complete positive-gap profile (2) are sharp.
Equality in (2) is attained by actual three-fiber convex bodies for
every p in [0,1]. If every fiber is required to have volume strictly
less than M/2, eta_d remains the optimal universal threshold and the
right side of (2) remains the supremal bound.

For d>=2 the threshold satisfies the useful uniform comparison

    eta_d>=39/64>1/2>Gamma_d,
    Gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d.                              (4)

In dimension one, B_1=3/2 and eta_1=1/4<Gamma_1=1/2.

## 2. The exact endpoint-volume envelope

The function x^d-(2-x)^d is continuous and strictly increasing on
[1,2], takes values zero and 2^d at its endpoints, and therefore
defines the unique B_d in (1).

Brunn--Minkowski and midpoint compatibility give a+b<=2c. Normalize
c=1 temporarily, and let b be the larger endpoint root after swapping
the endpoint labels if necessary. If b<=1, then b<B_d already.
Otherwise 1<b<2 and a<=2-b. The noheavy inequality for this endpoint is

    b^d<=1+a^d<=1+(2-b)^d.

Strict monotonicity in (1) gives b<=B_d. Undoing the normalization,

    max(a,b)<=B_d c.                                 (5)

Both steps can be equalities: take a=(2-B_d)c and b=B_d c with
homothetic fibers and equality in their Minkowski midpoint inclusion.
Thus this endpoint envelope is exact under the stated hypotheses.

## 3. Residual Brunn--Minkowski, with all boundary cases

Write the halfspace as H={L(z,x)>=0}, where L is a nonconstant affine
functional. Its strict residual in each fiber is {L(z,x)<0}. If this
residual is nonempty, it has positive d-volume: an interior point of
the full-dimensional fiber can be chosen sufficiently close to any
strictly residual point, and a small ball around it stays strict.
This also covers a purely integer normal, when each residual is
either an entire fiber or empty.

Suppose both endpoint residuals are nonempty. For sufficiently small
epsilon>0 the compact convex sets

    A_epsilon=A intersect {L(-1,x)<=-epsilon},
    R_epsilon=R intersect {L(1,x)<=-epsilon}

are nonempty. Midpoint compatibility and affinity give

    (A_epsilon+R_epsilon)/2
        subset K intersect {L(0,x)<=-epsilon}
        subset K minus H_0.

Brunn--Minkowski therefore yields

    f_0>=(|A_epsilon|^(1/d)+|R_epsilon|^(1/d))/2.

As epsilon decreases to zero these sets increase to the strict
endpoint residuals. Continuity from below of their finite volumes
proves (3). This argument neither substitutes closed residuals that
carry boundary mass nor applies Brunn--Minkowski to an empty set.

If one or both endpoint residuals are empty, at most one term among
f_-,f_+ is positive. By (5),

    (f_-+f_+)/2<=B_d c/2.

Subtract f_0=c(1-p)^(1/d) and take the positive part. This proves (2).
When both residuals were nonempty, the left side of (2) was zero,
so the same inequality holds. The implication (3) at p<=eta_d now
follows directly from the definition of eta_d.

## 4. Comparison with the continuous Grünbaum fraction

For d=2, equation (1) is 4B_2-4=1, so B_2=5/4 and

    eta_2=1-(5/8)^2=39/64.

For every integer d>=2,

    (5/4)^d-(3/4)^d
        >=(5/4)^2-(3/4)^2=1.

Consequently B_d<=5/4, and

    eta_d>=1-(5/8)^d>=1-(5/8)^2=39/64.

The binomial expansion for d>=2 gives

    (1+1/d)^d>1+d(1/d)=2,

so Gamma_d<1/2. This proves every inequality in (4), using exact
rational bounds rather than an asymptotic comparison.
For d=1 equation (1) gives B_1=3/2 and the stated eta_1=1/4.

Thus an actual original midpoint-row failure in d>=2 necessarily
has middle captured fraction strictly larger than 39/64, and in
particular strictly larger than Gamma_d. This conclusion concerns
the midpoint row and the three-fiber noheavy hypotheses only; it
does not apply to a general KKT row with more destinations.

## 5. Exact sharpness for every prescribed middle cap fraction

Choose any d-dimensional convex body T of volume one and put

    K=T, A=(2-B_d)T, R=B_d T.

Homotheties are about one fixed origin; it is not necessary that the
origin belong to T. Convexity gives

    (A+R)/2=T.

The lifted convex hull of these three fibers has projection [-1,1]
and exactly the indicated integer fibers: any mixture at base zero
combines T with endpoint midpoints already in T. It is a genuine
full-dimensional convex body in R times R^d.

Its larger endpoint volume is

    |R|=B_d^d=1+(2-B_d)^d=|K|+|A|=M/2.

The other two volumes are strictly smaller than M/2, so all noheavy
hypotheses hold. Fix any prescribed p in [0,1]. Choose a nonzero
continuous normal u and a finite threshold beta with

    |T intersect {u.x>=beta}|=p.

Existence follows from continuity and strict decrease of the cap
volume between the two supporting thresholds. The endpoint values
p=0 and p=1 use the upper and lower supporting thresholds; their
support faces have zero d-volume.

Choose a finite number L satisfying

    L>max{beta-min_A u.x, max_R u.x-beta, 0}.

The single actual ambient halfspace

    H={(z,x):u.x-Lz>=beta}

strictly captures all of A and strictly misses all of R. Its middle
captured fraction is exactly p. Therefore its residual roots are

    (f_-,f_0,f_+)=(0,(1-p)^(1/d),B_d).

Substitution gives equality in (2) for every p. In particular, any
p>eta_d violates (3), proving the sharp threshold.

For strict noheavy, replace B_d by t in (1,B_d), set A=(2-t)T,
and R=tT. Their midpoint is still exactly T. The larger endpoint
volume obeys t^d<1+(2-t)^d. The middle volume is strictly smaller
than the sum of the endpoints, since convexity of the power gives
(2-t)^d+t^d>=2>1. The remaining endpoint also satisfies its strict
noheavy inequality. The same cap construction gives gap

    [t/2-(1-p)^(1/d)]_+.

As t increases to B_d this converges to the sharp right side of (2).
For any fixed p>eta_d, it is positive for t sufficiently close to
B_d. Thus strict noheavy does not permit a larger threshold.

## 6. An equivalent exact excess-mass certificate

If an actual midpoint-row gap equals delta>0, (2) implies

    p>=1-(B_d/2-delta/c)^d>eta_d,
    0<delta/c<=B_d/2.                                (6)

Conversely the sharp family in Section 5 attains this curve. Hence
(6) quantifies the excess middle cap mass needed for each positive
row deficit. It does not claim that the excess can be charged once
across an arbitrary collection of caps or rows; such an additional
global comparison would require a separate proof.

## 7. Without noheavy: sharp growth and a forced heavy destination

Now DROP the noheavy assumption, retaining compatibility and positive
full-dimensional fiber volumes. Suppose d>=2, p<=Gamma_d, and the
original midpoint row fails strictly. Section 3 shows that exactly
one endpoint residual is nonempty. Call that endpoint R. Since

    f_+>2f_0=2c(1-p)^(1/d),

its FULL fiber volume satisfies the sharp strict growth estimate

    |R|>2^d(1-p)|K|
         >=lambda_d |K|,
    lambda_d=2^d(1-Gamma_d)>2^(d-1)>=2.               (7)

Moreover this same endpoint, rather than an unspecified one, is
locally heavy. Indeed p<=Gamma_d<eta_d gives b/c>B_d. Compatibility
gives a/c<=2-b/c. Strict monotonicity in (1) then implies

    |R|>|A|+|K|.                                    (8)

The factor 2^d(1-p) is optimal for each fixed p in (0,1), if one
does not impose noheavy. In the construction of Section 5 replace
B_d by any t with

    2(1-p)^(1/d)<t<2,

and keep the same prescribed cap fraction and full/empty endpoint
statuses. The row fails and |R|/|K|=t^d tends down to the claimed
factor as t tends down to 2(1-p)^(1/d). For p=0 a strict failure is
impossible by a+b<=2c, so this endpoint of the assertion is excluded.

These conclusions apply equally to any three full-dimensional
fibers of an actual mixed-integer convex body whose integer bases
are j,k,i=(j+k)/2: only the actual midpoint inclusion and affine
halfspace identity were used. If at every source base with a
chosen low-own-cap row failure one draws an edge toward its unique
positive-residual endpoint, fiber volume strictly increases by
more than lambda_d on every edge. Hence there are no directed
cycles. Choosing at most one such edge from each source gives a
directed forest on the finite set of positive fibers. A path of
h>=1 edges satisfies

    lambda_d^h |C_start|<|C_end|<=max_z |C_z|.

This is an exact termination mechanism. It does NOT bound how many
sources can point to one destination. The actual cone construction
in `candidate da1391b1383b9a0e`
shows that even global noheavy and globally below-OC source caps
permit arbitrarily large indegree and incoming source mass. Thus
termination alone is insufficient for a mass-charging argument.
